events.headline: Jadarian Price and Zach Charbonnet split Seattle's backfield in a 34-17 loss; Emanuel Wilson gets no carries
events.detail: Price had 10 carries for 29 yards and caught 2 of 4 targets for 8 yards. Charbonnet, in his first game since tearing his ACL in January, had 6 carries for 23 yards and caught 3 of 4 targets for 6 yards. They alternated starts on the first four drives, then Price played consecutive series and opened the second half, per Gregg Bell. Wilson, 100 yards eight days earlier against Kansas City, did not carry. George Holani took the two-minute work. Seattle's backs had 61 yards on 17 carries, with left tackle Charles Cross out. Mike Macdonald said the backs "came out OK." Wilson played seven snaps, all on special teams, per RotoWire. Charbonnet is still managing the knee.
events.so_what: Price has the small lead and Charbonnet's workload should grow, so neither is a safe start at home against Arizona in Week 9: the split is live and the blocking is short a left tackle. Wilson went from starter to no carries in one week, which makes him the drop among the three.

source.label: Gregg Bell, 93.3 KJR: Price, Charbonnet no spark in Seahawks' 34-17 loss (Nov. 3)

events.headline: Joe Fagnano named Ravens starter for Thursday with an ankle brace; Lamar Jackson (thumb) headed to IR, Tyler Huntley (turf toe) an IR candidate
events.detail: Jesse Minter confirmed Tuesday that the undrafted rookie starts against Jacksonville. Fagnano went 10 of 21 for 91 yards and an interception in the 36-10 loss, hurt his right ankle and practiced Tuesday in a heavy brace. Jackson injured his right thumb on his first pass back from a high ankle sprain and is headed for surgery and IR; Minter said it could be season-ending. Huntley missed practice and Minter called him a potential IR candidate. Baltimore signed Kedon Slovis off Green Bay's practice squad, added Austin Reed to its practice squad and worked out Adrian Martinez. Zay Flowers finished Sunday with no catches on five targets, and Derrick Henry has been under 60 rushing yards for three straight games.
events.so_what: Jackson is an IR stash at best and a drop if the season-ending read holds. Nobody at this quarterback spot is worth starting. That hits Flowers and Mark Andrews on TD odds, and RotoWire expects Baltimore to lean on Henry, who faces stacked boxes on a short week, so lower him as well. Thursday kickoff: these decisions lock early.

source.label: RotoWire: Joe Fagnano named Week 9 starter (Nov. 3)

events.headline: Jeremiyah Love on IR with a right high-ankle sprain, 4-to-5 weeks; Tyler Allgeier takes the lead role
events.detail: Arizona placed Love on injured reserve Tuesday, per Darren Urban, and Ian Rapoport reports a right high-ankle sprain with a 4-to-5 week recovery. IR means at least four games. It is his third ankle injury as a rookie. RotoWire expects Allgeier to lead the backfield starting at Seattle in Week 9, after Allgeier played all 40 second-half and overtime snaps per PFF with 11 carries for 147 yards and five catches for 44 yards, and a touchdown each way. Bam Knight is in the concussion protocol and could miss Week 9. Mike LaFleur said Tuesday that James Conner (foot, on IR and not cleared to practice) will not return this week, so Evan Hull is the primary backup if Knight sits.
events.so_what: Love goes to an IR slot if you have one, and that timeline points to a return around Week 13 or 14, so he is a hold rather than a drop. Allgeier is a start on volume now that the job is his for a month and Conner is no threat to it yet, but the 147 yards came largely on two long runs and Seattle is next, so expect RB2/FLEX production rather than a repeat. Conner stays an IR stash.

source.label: RotoWire: Jeremiyah Love hits IR, out 4-to-5 weeks (Nov. 3)

events.headline: Gardner Minshew named Cardinals starter for Week 9 at Seattle; Jacoby Brissett drops to No. 3 and Kendrick Bourne (tibia) goes on IR
events.detail: Mike LaFleur confirmed Monday that Minshew starts at Seattle with rookie Carson Beck as the backup and Brissett third. Brissett was benched late in the third quarter of Sunday's game (10 of 23, 119 yards, an interception), and Minshew went 17 of 23 for 188 yards and three touchdowns in the 33-30 overtime win at Dallas. Michael Wilson caught 8 of a team-high 15 targets for 111 yards while playing with broken ribs. Bourne (26 catches, 263 yards, no touchdowns) was placed on IR Tuesday with a season-ending fractured tibia that won't need surgery, per Adam Schefter. Jalen Brooks (wrist) is already out. Simi Fehoko is listed as a starting receiver on the unofficial depth chart, per Bo Brack of GoPHNX.com via RotoWire; he played 40 of 81 snaps at Dallas and had one catch for 17 yards.
events.so_what: Not a streamer yet: Seattle is next and a pocket quarterback at 4 points a pass TD has little floor. The useful part is Wilson, whose target count made him the receiver to start in this offense, provided the ribs hold up through the week. Bourne is a drop. Fehoko has the snaps but not the targets, with Trey McBride and Wilson ahead of him, so he is not worth a bid off a depth chart.

source.label: Yahoo Sports: NFL news live updates (Nov. 2-3)

events.headline: Jeremy McNichols on IR with a mid-foot injury and not expected back this season; Rachaad White and Austin Ekeler are Washington's backs
events.detail: Washington placed McNichols on IR Tuesday, along with defensive tackles Daron Payne and Javon Kinlaw. Tashan Reed of The Washington Post reports he isn't expected to play again this season, though he is seeking more medical opinions. With Jacory Croskey-Merritt also on IR, White and Ekeler were the only backs on the active roster, so Washington claimed Robert Henry off waivers from Seattle. Devin Neal and Craig Reynolds remain on the practice squad.
events.so_what: McNichols is a drop. White led the team in carries Sunday and moves up the FLEX list as the early-down back, with the Rams next; Ekeler gets the passing downs. Henry is depth, not a bid, until he gets a carry.

source.label: RotoWire: Jeremy McNichols heads to injured reserve (Nov. 3)

events.headline: Christian McCaffrey (hamstring), Mike Evans (Achilles) and Deebo Samuel (hamstring) all have a chance at Week 9 out of the 49ers bye; none confirmed
events.detail: McCaffrey missed the second quarter of the win over Atlanta with what was first called a thigh injury, and Kyle Shanahan said it was a mild hamstring strain. Yahoo's Monday report does not expect him to miss Week 9 at home against Las Vegas. Rookie Kaelon Black got expanded work and scored his first touchdown in the Atlanta game. Shanahan said Evans and Samuel, who has been out since Week 5, also have a chance to return after the bye. All three are on the Week 9 list with no designation yet, and San Francisco's first practice report comes Wednesday.
events.so_what: These are forecasts until the practice report. Start McCaffrey unless it says otherwise. Evans and Samuel returning would crowd a passing game that has run through McCaffrey and George Kittle, so don't start either off a chance-to-return quote, and expect Brandin Cooks and Jacob Cowing to lose work if they do come back.

source.label: DraftKings Network: NFL injury report for Week 9 (Nov. 3)

events.headline: Bhayshul Tuten (ankle, foot) sits out Tuesday, in doubt for Thursday at Baltimore; Chris Rodriguez and Jakobi Meyers limited
events.detail: Tuten was a non-participant for a second straight day with two lower-body injuries from Sunday's win over Indianapolis, and wasn't seen in the media-viewable part of practice. RotoWire says practicing in some form Wednesday would put him in a good spot to play. Chris Rodriguez Jr. (hand) was limited and is the top candidate to lead the ground game if Tuten sits. Meyers (hamstring, ankle) was limited and may need a full practice Wednesday to avoid a designation.
events.so_what: Thursday kickoff, so this needs an answer by Wednesday night's report. If Tuten is out, Rodriguez is a volume RB2 against a Ravens team that may not hold many leads with a rookie at quarterback. Have a backup plan for Meyers rather than waiting on a designation.

source.label: RotoWire: Bhayshul Tuten sits out Tuesday's practice (Nov. 3)

events.headline: Two kicker jobs change: Tyler Loop (groin) on IR with Jake Moody up in Baltimore; Saints cut Daniel Carlson and plan to use Charlie Smyth
events.detail: Baltimore placed Loop on IR Tuesday and expects to use Moody, on the practice squad since Oct. 20, on Thursday. New Orleans released Carlson, whose 66.7% field-goal rate is a career low, and plans to elevate or sign Smyth from the practice squad for Sunday against Cleveland, per Ross Jackson of WWL Louisiana. Smyth kicked the final six games last season and went 12 of 16 on field goals and 13 of 13 on extra points, with two of the misses from beyond 50.
events.so_what: Loop and Carlson are drops. Moody isn't worth a claim behind a rookie quarterback who will stall drives short of field-goal range, and with misses costing points a shaky new kicker is a poor stream. Smyth is in line for the job, but he is a one-week matchup stream at most until he shows more than last year's 12 of 16.

source.label: RotoWire: Charlie Smyth set to kick for Saints in Week 9 (Nov. 3)

events.headline: Rashid Shaheed (knee) has "a chance" to play Sunday against Arizona, says Macdonald
events.detail: Shaheed missed Monday's 34-17 loss to Chicago, his first absence of the season, after not practicing all week. Tory Horton took more snaps as the No. 3 receiver behind Jaxon Smith-Njigba and Cooper Kupp. RotoWire says he may need a full practice to be ready.
events.so_what: A chance is not a clearance, so leave him on the bench until he practices fully. His value is big plays, and a knee is a poor fit for that. Horton's snaps last only as long as Shaheed is out.

source.label: RotoWire: Rashid Shaheed iffy for Week 9 (Nov. 3)

events.headline: Jordyn Tyson could play as soon as Week 9, per Schefter, and Travis Etienne Jr. (hamstring) could open his IR window Wednesday; Saints claim Audric Estime
events.detail: Adam Schefter reported Tuesday that Tyson, the Saints' first-round pick, could return against Cleveland, per Pro Football Rumors. His practice window had not opened as of Tuesday and could open Wednesday; a mid-August hamstring injury and setbacks have kept him out, and he traveled with the team to Paris in Week 7. Kellen Moore said Etienne would be evaluated Monday before a decision on practice, per WWL's Ross Jackson via RotoWire. Etienne has been out since Sept. 27 and is eligible after the Week 8 bye. New Orleans also claimed Estime off waivers from Cleveland; he starts as depth behind Alvin Kamara, Kendre Miller and CJ Donaldson, who has a shoulder injury.
events.so_what: An opened window is not an activation, so neither is a Week 9 start off these reports. Tyson is a stash until he is on the active list and has a practice week behind him. If Etienne is on your wire or a rival's IR, plan around Week 10. Estime is not a bid unless the backs ahead of him start missing games.

source.label: Pro Football Rumors: WR notes, Tyson could play Week 9 (Nov. 3)

events.headline: Saquon Barkley on a pitch count with hamstring and back and will not be traded, per ESPN; DeVonta Smith (hamstring) sat Week 8; Sirianni keeps Tanner McKee and play-caller Sean Mannion
events.detail: Barkley played against Washington but ran 13 times for 30 yards and a touchdown in a 27-10 loss, with his body "not really where I need [it] to be," he said after the game. ESPN reported Monday that he will not be moved before the Nov. 10 deadline. DeVonta Smith was inactive with a hamstring injury and there was no update on his return. Philadelphia is 2-6 and starting Tanner McKee, with the Giants next. Nick Sirianni said after the sixth straight loss that Mannion keeps calling plays ("I'm not making any changes there") and that McKee stays the starter, per Pro Football Rumors.
events.so_what: Played is not the same as healthy. The touchdown saved the day, and a split with Elijah Mitchell behind this offense makes Barkley a risky RB2 until he practices fully. Neither a trade nor a new play-caller is coming to rescue his role, so value him as an Eagle in the same offense. Smith needs a practice report before he starts anywhere.

source.label: Philadelphia Inquirer: Eagles live updates, injuries and trade deadline (Nov. 2)

events.headline: Brian Thomas Jr. draws trade interest from several teams before the Nov. 10 deadline; Steelers linked to him and Josh Downs, with Michael Pittman Jr. no closer to returning
events.detail: Ian Rapoport reports several teams have asked about Thomas, per RotoWire, though it is unclear whether Jacksonville wants to sell. He has played behind Parker Washington and Jakobi Meyers in snap share and has topped three targets in only one of seven games. Pittsburgh has been linked to Thomas and Downs, per Pro Football Rumors. Pittman has been on IR since Week 4 and said the plantar fasciitis "morphed into something else"; he only recently resumed running and has no timetable.
events.so_what: Thomas is a free roll on a landing spot rather than a start: his current role doesn't justify a lineup slot, but a move into a thinner receiver room would change that fast. Worth a bench spot only if yours is otherwise idle, given how short benches are. Pittman is a drop candidate unless you have an open IR slot.

source.label: RotoWire: Brian Thomas appealing trade target for number of teams (Nov. 3)

events.headline: Jake Ferguson has a low ankle sprain after leaving Sunday on the first drive
events.detail: ESPN's Jeremy Fowler reports a low ankle sprain, with no timetable given. Ferguson exited on Dallas' first possession against Arizona without a catch. With Luke Schoonmaker (groin) inactive, Brevyn Spann-Ford played most of the remaining snaps and James Mitchell was elevated. Dallas plays at Indianapolis in Week 9.
events.so_what: A low sprain is the better version of this injury, but treat him as week-to-week until he practices. Have a Week 9 tight end ready; Spann-Ford inherits snaps, not a proven target share, so he is a last resort rather than a bid.

source.label: Yahoo Sports: Cowboys hit with troubling Jake Ferguson injury update (Nov. 2)

events.headline: Steichen sticks with Daniel Jones for Week 9 vs. Dallas after pulling him in a 42-7 loss
events.detail: Shane Steichen said Monday, "I do feel that Daniel gives us the best chance to win right now," and that the offense's problems go beyond Jones, who has nine interceptions and a 39.6 QBR. He went 19 of 28 for 144 yards, a touchdown and two interceptions at Jacksonville, one of them off a Tyler Warren drop returned for a touchdown. Anthony Richardson relieved him with 11:53 left, down 35, and Steichen said that was about the score.
events.so_what: Richardson stays a stash, nothing more, and the "right now" is the part to watch. A start would change his value, because his rushing scores at RB rates under the konami premium. Jones is not a streamer, and the Colts receivers keep a low floor at home against Dallas.

source.label: ESPN: Shane Steichen sticking with Daniel Jones as Colts' QB1 for Week 9 (Nov. 2)

events.headline: Breece Hall (quad) expected back for Week 9 vs. Kansas City per Yahoo, after Braelon Allen ran for 147
events.detail: Hall was inactive against Las Vegas, his fifth straight missed game, and Allen rushed for a career-high 147 yards, his third 100-yard game since taking over, per ESPN. Yahoo's Monday injury report expects Hall back against Kansas City and expects a split. The team has not confirmed it and no practice report exists yet. Trade speculation around him continues ahead of the Nov. 10 deadline.
events.so_what: This is a forecast until he practices. If Hall returns, the job is a real question rather than an automatic handback, so both become RB2/FLEX options with a lower ceiling than Allen has had. Wait for Wednesday's report before starting Hall over a settled option.

source.label: Yahoo Sports: NFL Injury Report, Week 9 (Nov. 2)

events.headline: Packers expect Josh Jacobs to stay as the NFL reviews new abuse allegations he denies
events.detail: The league said Saturday it will review allegations disclosed in a public records release Friday night as part of its open investigation, per ESPN. Jacobs denied them, and his attorneys called them old hearsay. Green Bay expects him to remain with the team, per Ryan Wood via RotoWire. He pleaded no contest to two misdemeanor charges in September. No status change or timeline has been reported. He played 71% of the snaps in Thursday's win over Carolina, per Packers On SI; MarShawn Lloyd played 11 snaps.
events.so_what: He remains eligible and the team is not moving on, so lineups don't change today. Any discipline would land with little warning, and Lloyd is the back to look at as insurance if you roster Jacobs.

source.label: RotoWire: Josh Jacobs expected to remain with team (Nov. 2)

events.headline: Kyler Murray (hamstring) being evaluated; O'Connell says "I don't think we're there yet" on Week 9
events.detail: Murray is undergoing a full evaluation of a sore hamstring, per The Athletic's Alec Lewis via RotoWire. More on his status for next Monday's game against Buffalo is expected by Thursday's practice report. Carson Wentz is next in line if he sits.
events.so_what: A hamstring is the injury that takes away a rushing quarterback's konami value even if he plays, so a healthy-looking start can still score below his usual floor. Line up a streamer if you start him, since the Monday kickoff leaves no pivot once Sunday passes.

source.label: RotoWire: Kyler Murray undergoing evaluation on hamstring injury (Nov. 2)

events.headline: Cam Skattebo (hamstring) day-to-day, could be a game-time call vs. Philadelphia
events.detail: John Harbaugh said Skattebo is "day-to-day and could end up being a game-time decision" for Sunday, per ESPN's Jordan Raanan via RotoWire. He worked off to the side in Monday's unofficial practice coming out of the bye. Devin Singletary is next up, with Tyrone Tracy Jr. on IR.
events.so_what: Check for a practice jump by Friday, and have a Sunday-early alternative ready if he stays a game-time call. Singletary is the one-week add if you roster Skattebo, as a volume start rather than a bid worth chasing.

source.label: RotoWire: Cam Skattebo could be game-time call for Week 9 (Nov. 2)

events.headline: Christian Watson playing through a broken rib is undecided for Week 9 vs. New England
events.detail: Passing game coordinator Jason Vrable said Monday that Watson is sore but "doing great," adding "we'll see as the week goes," per The Athletic's Matt Schneidman via RotoWire. He broke a rib in Thursday's win over Carolina. Savion Williams, Bo Melton and J. Michael Sturdivant would get more snaps behind Matthew Golden if he sits.
events.so_what: Even if active he carries an early-exit risk, and that's a poor bet in a boom-or-bust role. Treat him as a bench piece until he practices fully. Golden is the Packers receiver who gains the most if Watson sits.

source.label: RotoWire: Christian Watson managing rib soreness ahead of Week 9 (Nov. 2)

events.headline: Matthew Stafford has soreness in his throwing arm; McVay won't say much before the first practice report
events.detail: Stafford left the locker room after Sunday's 24-9 win over the Chargers with ice on his right elbow, per Adam Grosbard of the LA Daily News. Sean McVay acknowledged some soreness Monday and deferred to Stafford on how he feels. He hasn't missed a snap to injury this year. The Rams play at Washington on Sunday, and Washington just put defensive tackles Daron Payne and Javon Kinlaw on IR.
events.so_what: No reason to bench him yet, and the matchup got easier, but an arm issue affects a pocket quarterback's deep throws before it costs him a game. Read Wednesday's report for his participation. Puka Nacua's volume is the safer Rams bet with Davante Adams on IR.

source.label: Yahoo Sports: Rams QB Matthew Stafford dealing with soreness in throwing arm (Nov. 2)

events.headline: Ashton Jeanty gets two carries as Mike Washington Jr. takes 25; Kubiak says it was 'my call'
events.detail: In the Raiders' 38-33 win over the Jets, Mike Washington Jr. started, carried 25 times for 83 yards (3.3 per carry, stuffed six times per ESPN), took early-down and goal-line work, and played 63% of the snaps to Jeanty's 37%. Jeanty ran twice for 9 yards and caught three passes for 64 yards as the receiving back. Klint Kubiak said, "That's my call, and Ashton is still going to be a big part of our team," and that Jeanty's pregame comments about the Jets were not a factor. Jeanty said he was told during the week that Washington would get more work. No starter has been named for Week 9 at San Francisco.
events.so_what: A planned role change matters more than Washington's inefficient 3.3 a carry. Washington has early-down and goal-line work, which is where TD points live, so he is a live FLEX. Jeanty is a matchup start on receiving yards until Kubiak shows the carries are coming back. ESPN expects a rebound; the Kubiak quote does not promise one.

source.label: Yahoo Sports: Klint Kubiak explains Ashton Jeanty's decreased role vs. Jets (Nov. 1)

events.headline: Jonathan Taylor trade talks stay live after his fewest carries since 2023; Josh Downs has already asked out
events.detail: ESPN and NFL Network reported Indianapolis is willing to move Taylor and has talked with the Broncos, Packers, Vikings, Giants and Seahawks; Taylor has not requested a trade. He played Sunday and had eight carries in the 42-7 loss to Jacksonville, his fewest since October 2023. Steichen blamed the score ("It wasn't like we had a number on his carries"), and Taylor called his game "nowhere near up to par." Josh Downs asked to be traded earlier in the week and played 89.6% of the snaps before garbage time per PFF. The reports conflict on heat: CBS' Aditi Kinkhabwala was assured the Colts are not soliciting offers. The deadline is Nov. 10.
events.so_what: One blowout does not change Taylor's value; a landing spot could. He stays a start while a Colt, with Dallas next, but a trade into a shared backfield costs touches and a move would make Seth McGowan the speculative stash. Downs is a hold pending a destination.

source.label: ESPN: Colts' Shane Steichen to 'evaluate everything,' including QB (Nov. 1)

events.headline: DJ Moore (knee) hurt late in his return, says it is not serious; Joshua Palmer (hamstring) ruled out
events.detail: Moore had his best game since Week 1 in the win over Baltimore, then hurt his knee late; he says it is not serious and his status will be monitored, per ESPN. Palmer left with a hamstring injury and was ruled out, per PFF. Dalton Kincaid (chest), also active after a Questionable tag, caught four passes for 86 yards and a touchdown. Buffalo faces Minnesota in Week 9.
events.so_what: Moore's own word is not a clearance, so wait for the Wednesday practice report before counting on him. If he or Palmer misses time, Keon Coleman and Khalil Shakir get the snaps. Kincaid stays locked in at a scarce position.

source.label: ESPN: Week 8 fantasy winners and losers (Nov. 1)

events.headline: Jonah Coleman takes over the Broncos backfield with RJ Harvey on IR and J.K. Dobbins fading
events.detail: Coleman led the backfield for a second straight week with a 68% snap rate, 11 carries for 41 yards and a touchdown, and four catches for 63 yards. He ran 16 routes, played 19 of 21 second-half snaps per PFF, and scored the go-ahead touchdown against Kansas City. Dobbins averaged 1.9 yards per carry. Harvey went on IR Saturday with a knee injury and is eligible no earlier than Week 13.
events.so_what: This is a lead-back role with routes attached, and Harvey's absence removes a competitor for at least four more games. Coleman is a weekly RB2/FLEX start and the top priority if still on your wire. Dobbins is a bench hold on goal-line hopes only.

source.label: ESPN: Week 8 fantasy winners and losers (Nov. 1)

events.headline: A.J. Brown and TreVeyon Henderson sat at Miami and Hunter Henry (foot) left; Rhamondre Stevenson played 77% of snaps
events.detail: Both were downgraded to out on Saturday, Brown (ankle, knee) after sitting out Thursday and Friday and Henderson with an illness. Stevenson played 77% of the offensive snaps per PFF, with Corey Kiner the primary backup. Efton Chism III led the team with five catches, and DeMario Douglas and Kyle Williams each scored from long range. Romeo Doubs and Mack Hollins are on IR. Henry was ruled out during the game with a foot injury, and rookie Eli Raridon played 92% of the snaps with one catch for five yards.
events.so_what: Week 9 against Green Bay turns on the Wednesday report for both. Henderson's illness should clear quicker than Brown's knee, which has been flaring. Stevenson is a FLEX if Henderson sits again; Douglas is a one-week add at most. Henry is uncertain until the practice report, and Raridon's snap count has not yet become targets, so he is a last-resort add at tight end.

source.label: PFF: Week 8 recap, immediate fantasy takeaways from Sunday's games (Nov. 1)
